components.name: Button
components.summary: Triggers an action or navigates, with a spring-loaded press.
components.description:
The button is the library's reference component: eleven variants, six sizes and five shapes.

It renders a native `<button>` — or an `<a>` when you pass `href` — and forwards every attribute and event to it. Pressing it drives a real spring through the motion channel rather than a CSS keyframe, so a quick tap and a long hold both feel right.

features: Eleven variants, five sizes, five shapes — shared with every other control
Leading and trailing icons from @fractaldesign/icons, plus leading and trailing snippets
Loading state that keeps the layout stable
Renders a link when given href; a disabled link stays an anchor with aria-disabled
Interruptible spring press, disabled under reduced motion
accessibility: Renders a native <button>, or an <a> when href is set. A disabled or loading link keeps the <a>, drops href, and sets aria-disabled and tabindex="-1".
While loading, the button is disabled and exposes aria-busy="true".
An icon-only button needs an aria-label; icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
The focus ring is drawn only for keyboard focus (:focus-visible).

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.summary: Joins related buttons into one segmented control, or spaces them evenly.
components.description:
A button group is layout, not behaviour: it lines its children up on one axis and, when `attached`, squares the inner corners and overlaps the hairlines so the buttons read as a single control. Each child keeps its own variant, size and handlers.

Give the group a `label` so assistive technology announces what the buttons have in common. For single or multiple selection, reach for `ToggleGroup` instead.

Horizontal or vertical
Hovered and focused buttons rise above their neighbours so rings are never clipped
Works with Button, IconButton and SplitButton children

Every child remains an independent tab stop.

components.name: CopyButton
components.summary: Copies text to the clipboard and confirms it with a spring-morphed check.
components.description:
The copy button writes `text` to the clipboard and answers with a small, unmistakable change: the copy glyph shrinks away and a check springs in, then everything settles back after `timeout`.

It is icon-only by default; give it children to show a visible label that swaps to `copiedLabel`. The result is announced politely to screen readers through a live region, so the confirmation is never visual-only.

Screen-reader announcement through an aria-live region
Icon-only or labelled copy trigger
onCopy callback with the copied text
Shares variants, sizes and shapes with Button

After a copy, copiedLabel is announced through a polite live region (role="status").
Does nothing, and announces nothing, if the browser refuses the clipboard write.
The clipboard API needs a secure context (HTTPS or localhost).

components.name: SplitButton
components.summary: A primary action with an attached menu of related alternatives.
components.description:

The menu is a native popover: it renders in the top layer, dismisses on Escape or an outside click, and returns focus to the chevron. It is positioned with CSS anchor positioning against the whole control, so it lines up with the outer edge whatever the label width.

Rows with icons, disabled and danger states
Roving keyboard navigation with typeahead

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A group of controls with one tab stop and arrow-key movement, following the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern.
components.description:
A toolbar gathers the actions of a view — an editor's formatting strip, a preview's zoom and layout switches — into one tab stop. Arrow keys move between the buttons, toggles and links inside; Tab leaves the toolbar entirely.

Existing action components drop in as children: `Button`, `IconButton`, `Toggle` and `Link`. Join a cluster of related controls with `ToolbarGroup`, which is a visual grouping only — it does not attach its own roving tabindex, so the toolbar remains the sole keyboard manager. Prefer it over `ToggleGroup` here: `ToggleGroup` already moves focus with the arrow keys, and the two would fight.

components.name: Field
components.summary: The form-field wrapper: a label, a control, helper text and an error, wired together for assistive technology.
components.description:
`Field` owns the plumbing every form control needs. It generates ids, renders a real `<label for>`, puts the hint or error under the control, and shares the result with whatever sits inside through context.

Every control in this kit reads that context on its own: the `id` matches the label, `aria-describedby` points at the hint or error, `aria-invalid` follows the error, and `required` and `disabled` carry through. `size`, `shape` and `variant` are inherited the same way, so a field can set the variant of the control inside it; the control's own props still win. To build your own control, call `useFieldControl()` — or read `getFieldContext()` directly — during initialisation.

Use `orientation="horizontal"` for settings pages where labels line up in a column to the left.

features: Label, hint and error with generated, stable ids
Controls pick ids, invalid state and variant (size, shape, surface) up through context
Error replaces the hint and is announced politely
Vertical and horizontal layouts
getFieldContext() and useFieldControl() for custom controls
accessibility: The label is a native <label> whose for attribute matches the control id, so clicking it focuses the control.
Hint and error text are linked to the control with aria-describedby, and the error is inside an aria-live="polite" region.
The control receives aria-invalid when there is an error and required when marked required.
Grouped controls (pin input, file drop) are named through aria-labelledby using the label id.

components.name: FileDrop
components.summary: A drag-and-drop zone with click-to-browse, a file list, and clear reasons when a file is rejected.
components.description:
Drop files onto the zone or click it to open the system picker. Accepted files appear in a list with their size and a remove button. Files that do not match `accept`, that are larger than `maxSize`, or that would take the list past `maxFiles` are refused, and the reason is shown under the list.

`multiple` is on by default; turn it off to keep a single file, replacing whatever was there. The value is a bindable `File[]`, also reported through `onFiles`. Inside a `Field`, the zone takes the label, description and invalid state from context.

Each remove button has an accessible name (Remove invoice.pdf, and so on).

components.name: Input
components.summary: A single-line text input in a framed field, with icons, prefixes, suffixes and a clear button.
components.description:
`Input` is the base of the text-entry kit. The visible box is a `.field` frame and the native `<input>` inside it is bare, so the frame — not the browser — draws the focus ring, and leading and trailing content sits inside the same border.

Inside a `Field` it takes its `id`, description, invalid and required state from context. Outside one, pass them yourself. Every other attribute (`type`, `placeholder`, `name`, `autocomplete`, `inputmode`, event handlers) goes to the native input; `class` goes to the frame.

The value is bindable and also reported through `onValueChange`, so it works controlled or uncontrolled.

features: Three variants, five sizes and five shapes — the same axes as Button
Leading icon, leading and trailing snippets
Clearable, with a spring-in clear button and Escape to clear
Joins a Field automatically
Frame-level focus ring and invalid styling
accessibility: Renders a native <input>; label, description and error come from Field via for, aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology. The clear button has an accessible name and stays out of the tab order, because Escape does the same job.
Without a Field, give the input an aria-label or associate a <label> yourself.
The focus ring is drawn on the frame with :focus-within, so it is visible for keyboard and pointer focus alike.

Moves focus into and out of the field.

components.description:

Press and hold a stepper to repeat. Inside a `Field` it takes its id, description and invalid state from context.

components.name: PinInput
components.summary: A row of cells for one-time codes and PINs, with paste distribution, auto-advance, and a spring pop as each cell fills.
components.description:
Each cell is a single character of a code. Typing advances to the next cell; Backspace on an empty cell returns to the previous one and clears it. Pasting a code (from an SMS, a password manager, the clipboard) distributes characters across the cells from the caret.

The first cell carries `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so platforms that offer a received code can fill the group in one step. `type="numeric"` accepts digits only; `alphanumeric` accepts letters too. `mask` hides the characters. A filled cell pops with a spring.

Inside a `Field`, the group is named by the label (`aria-labelledby`) and the first cell receives the label's `for`.

The first input has autocomplete="one-time-code" and carries the Field id, so clicking the label focuses it.
aria-invalid and aria-describedby are applied to the group and to each cell.
mask uses type="password" on every cell, so assistive technology does not read the code aloud as it is typed.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.summary: A confirmation dialog that requires a choice, with an imperative confirm() helper.
components.description:
An alert dialog is a modal that cannot be dismissed by Esc or a click on the backdrop — the person has to choose. Focus lands on the cancel action, the least destructive choice, and the confirm action takes its colour from `tone`.

If `onConfirm` returns a promise, the confirm button stays in a loading state until it settles. Returning `false` keeps the dialog open.

For confirmations that are not tied to a particular trigger, mount `<Confirmer />` once and call `confirm({ title, description, … })`, which returns a `Promise<boolean>`.

Focus lands on the cancel action
Async onConfirm with a loading state
Imperative confirm() API with a Confirmer host

Esc and a click on the backdrop do not close it; a choice is required.
Focus moves to the cancel action when the dialog opens — the least destructive choice.
The title is the accessible name and the description is the accessible description.

components.name: Dialog

components.description:

components.name: Popover
components.summary: An anchored non-modal panel on the Popover API, placed with CSS anchor positioning.
components.description:
The panel is a native popover — top layer, no portal, no z-index. CSS anchor positioning places it against the trigger, and `.pop` springs it in from the trigger's side.

`trigger="click"` toggles the panel and light-dismisses it (a click outside or Esc). `trigger="hover"` opens on hover or focus and stays open while the pointer travels to the panel. `trigger="manual"` is driven only by binding `open`.

The opener is the `target` snippet — `trigger` is the open mode. Spread `props` onto your own button. An arrow is not offered: CSS anchor positioning has no clean way to draw one from registered classes.

Optional match-width and a configurable offset
Focus moves into the panel on click and returns to the trigger on close
accessibility: A click popover has role="dialog". The trigger carries aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded and aria-controls.
On click open, focus moves to the panel; on close, it returns to the trigger.
Esc and a click outside dismiss a click popover (popover="auto").
A hover popover does not move focus and is dismissed when hover or focus leaves the trigger and the panel.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short hint on hover or focus, using popover="hint" and a shared warm group.
components.description:
A tooltip describes a control when the pointer hovers it or the control is focused. It uses `popover="hint"` where the engine supports it, and falls back to `popover="manual"` otherwise — it never traps pointer or focus. Esc dismisses it.

Neighbouring tooltips share a warm group: after one has opened, the next opens instantly, so a row of icon buttons does not feel laggy. `delay` and `closeDelay` are in milliseconds.

The trigger receives `aria-describedby` pointing at the hint while it is open.

Esc dismisses; the hint never traps the pointer

The hint carries pointer-events: none, so it never intercepts the pointer.
Focus stays on the trigger; the hint does not take focus.
Esc closes the hint.

components.name: NavigationMenu
components.summary: A site navigation with delayed flyout panels, a sliding indicator, and a viewport that springs between sizes.
components.description:
A navigation menu is the primary site nav: a row of triggers that open rich flyout panels, mixed with ordinary links. Hovering a trigger opens its panel after a short delay; once one panel is open the menu is warm, and moving to the next trigger opens instantly. The open trigger is marked by a sliding indicator, and every panel shares one viewport whose box springs to the measured size of the active content.

The viewport is a native popover anchored to the list. `NavigationMenuContent` is portaled into that viewport, so the call site stays next to its trigger while the surface itself is shared. The library stays router-agnostic: pass `href` and `current` as props, and never import the SvelteKit app module.

components.name: Tabs

The parts share context: wrap a `TabList` of `Tab`s and matching `TabPanel`s in `Tabs`. Arrow keys move a roving tabindex; automatic activation selects on focus, manual waits for Enter or Space.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: An inline message that tells people something about the page they are on.
components.description:
The alert sits in the flow of the page, next to the thing it is about. It takes a `tone` for what it means and a `variant` for how loudly it says it: a quiet tinted fill, a hairline outline, or a solid block.

Each tone brings its own icon, and a title, a body and a row of actions can be stacked inside. A dismissible alert springs closed and collapses its own height, so the content beneath it glides up rather than jumping.

features: Five tones and three variants, shared with the rest of the status vocabulary
A default icon per tone, replaceable or removable
Springs closed and collapses its height when dismissed
An actions slot for buttons and links
accessibility: Danger and warning alerts use role="alert", so assistive technology announces them immediately.
Info, success and neutral alerts use role="status", a polite live region announced when the reader is idle.
Pass your own role to override the default, for example role="note" for static content that is present on load.
Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the tone is never conveyed by colour alone, because the title and message carry the meaning.
The dismiss button is a native button labelled "Dismiss" with a visible keyboard focus ring.

Dismisses the alert when the dismiss button is focused.

components.name: Banner
components.summary: A full-width announcement for the page or the site, optionally pinned and remembered when dismissed.
components.description:
A banner sits at the edge of the page — a release note, a billing reminder, a status change — and stretches the full width of its container. It shares the five tones of the rest of the status vocabulary.

When `sticky` is set, the banner pins to the top of the scrollport as the page moves. A dismissible banner can be given a `storageKey`: the dismissal is written to `localStorage`, so the same announcement does not come back on the next visit.

Pass your own role to override the default.
Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the title and message carry the meaning.
The dismiss button is a native button labelled "Dismiss" with a visible keyboard focus ring.

components.name: Meter
components.summary: A gauge for a value on a known range, with optional low, high and optimum thresholds.
components.description:
A meter is not a progress bar. Progress tells you how far a task has come; a meter tells you where a value sits on a scale — disk used, battery left, a score out of ten.

The fill uses the same `--value` channel as Progress, and the optional ring is the same conic fill as ProgressRing. When you set `low`, `high` and `optimum`, the tone is picked with the HTML `<meter>` region rules: the optimum region is success, the neighbouring region is warning, and the far region is danger. Pass `tone` to choose the colour yourself.

Five sizes and three ring thicknesses

Pass label to give the meter an accessible name; the visible label and the accessible name are the same string.

components.name: Toast
components.summary: An imperative notification, stacked in a pile at the edge of the viewport.
components.description:
Call `toast()` from anywhere in the app — after a save, a failure, a long job. A single `<Toaster />`, mounted near the root, draws the pile in the top layer through a manual popover.

The pile collapses into a stacked peek and expands on hover or focus, or stays open when `expand` is set. New toasts spring in from the nearest edge, a swipe with enough distance or velocity dismisses one, and the rest reflow with a FLIP spring. Timers pause while the pile is hovered, focused, or the tab is hidden. Passing an existing `id` updates a toast in place, which is how `toast.promise` moves from loading to success or error.

parts.Toaster: The host that renders the pile. Mount once near the root of the app.

Update in place by id, and dismiss one or all

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A portrait that falls back from an image to initials, then to an icon, with an optional status dot.
components.description:
An avatar is a compact, named likeness. Give it a photograph and it crops the image to the tile; if the image is missing or fails to load, it draws initials from the person's name on a colour derived from that name — a hue written to a custom property, never a hard-coded colour. With no name either, it shows a user icon.

A status dot marks presence: online, away, busy or offline. Sizes follow the shared ladder; the shape is a circle, a rounded square or a square.

Five sizes and three shapes

The photograph, initials and icon are decorative; assistive technology hears only the accessible name.
The status dot is colour and position, and is also included in the accessible name so it is not conveyed by colour alone.

components.name: Card
components.summary: The content surface: a padded container with five treatments and an optional spring lift.
components.description:
A card groups related content on a surface. It is built from parts (header, title, description, content, footer and edge-to-edge media) that take their padding, gap and type scale from the card's `size`, so a card always has the same rhythm.

Five variants cover the range from a raised, lit `elevated` panel to a `ghost` card that only appears under the pointer. Give it `href` or `interactive` and the whole card becomes a target that lifts on a spring; `tilt` swaps the lift for a 3D lean toward the pointer.

An interactive card without href is a focusable <article role="button"> and activates on Enter and Space.
Do not nest links or buttons inside a card that is itself a link or button.
CardTitle renders a real heading; choose level to keep the page outline correct.
The focus ring is drawn only for keyboard focus (:focus-visible).

components.name: AspectFrame
components.summary: A box of fixed proportion that holds media and clips it to its shape.
components.description:
An aspect frame reserves a box of a fixed proportion before its media arrives, so a grid of images or videos keeps its rhythm while it loads and never shifts the layout around it.

The frame does not own the media. It hands the media a class through the children snippet, and that class fills the frame and applies the fit: cover crops to fill, contain letterboxes, fill stretches, scale-down never enlarges past the natural size. Put the image or video in the snippet and bind the class to it.

Four fits, applied to the media through the children snippet
Five shapes, clipping the media to the corner radius
No layout shift while the media loads
accessibility: The frame is a plain div and carries no role; the media inside it carries the meaning.
Give every img an alt text that describes what it shows, or an empty alt when the image is decorative.
Video inside a frame needs its own captions and controls; the frame does not add them.

`Carousel` is a horizontal rail of `CarouselSlide`s, built on fractalstyler's `.reel` and `.carousel-track`. Slides snap into place, `perView` and `gap` travel as custom properties, and a pair of buttons plus a row of dots move the current index. The active dot is followed by a spring `.indicator`.

Drag the track to scroll with momentum; it snaps to the nearest slide on release. Autoplay advances on a timer and pauses while the carousel is hovered, focused, or the user prefers reduced motion. Keyboard arrows, Home and End move the rail, and a polite live region announces the current slide.

A visually hidden live region politely announces the current slide when the index changes.

Bind `open` to control it, or leave it uncontrolled. Disable the trigger when the content is not ready. Reach for `Accordion` when several disclosures need to coordinate.

components.name: DataTable
components.summary: A data grid with client-side sort, filter, selection, pagination and expandable rows.
components.description:
`DataTable` is the interactive counterpart to `Table`. You hand it columns and rows, generic over the row type, and it sorts, filters and pages them on the client. Multi-column sort is a shift-click on a header — the caret springs to the new direction, and the rows reflow with FLIP so a reorder is something you can follow with your eye.

Selection is a tri-state checkbox in the header, with shift-click ranges down the body. A built-in pager, a filter field, a columns menu and optional expandable detail rows (the same `.collapse` used by Accordion) sit around the same quiet table typography: tabular numerals, uppercase headers, hairline rows. Reach for `Table` when you already have the rows you want to show.

features: Generic over the row type, with typed column accessors and cell snippets
Multi-column sort with a spring caret and FLIP row reflow
Global filter text plus optional per-column filter functions
Row selection with a tri-state header checkbox and shift-click ranges
Pagination with its own pager, loading skeletons and an empty state
Expandable detail rows, column visibility, sticky header

Sortable headers are buttons that expose aria-sort (ascending, descending, or none).
The header checkbox is labelled "Select all rows on this page" and becomes indeterminate when the page is partly selected.
Each row checkbox and expand control is labelled. The filter field and columns menu are labelled too.
Give the table a caption or a label so assistive technology can name the grid.

Activates the focused control (sort, checkbox, expand, page).
On a sortable header, adds the column to the sort. On a row checkbox, selects the range from the last clicked row.
Scroll the labelled table region when it overflows.

components.name: Table
components.summary: A presentational table of records with quiet headers, hairline rows and aligned numerals.
components.description:
`Table` is the semantic HTML table, dressed in fractalstyler's `.data-table`: a quiet uppercase header row, hairline separators, an optional zebra stripe and a row hover. Its parts map one-to-one onto the native elements, so screen readers announce rows, columns and headers without any extra wiring.

The table sits in its own scroll container, so a wide table scrolls sideways instead of breaking the page; give it `maxHeight` and `stickyHeader` and the header stays in view while the body scrolls. Mark number columns `numeric` — on both the header and the cells — and the digits right-align on tabular numerals so they read down the column.

Reach for `DataTable` when you need sorting, filtering, selection or pagination; reach for `Table` when you already have the rows you want to show.

parts.TableBody: The body section (<tbody>) — holds the data rows.
parts.TableRow: A row (<tr>); `selected` gives it the selected fill.
parts.TableHeader: A header cell (<th scope="col">) with alignment, numeric and width helpers.
parts.TableCell: A data cell (<td>) with alignment, numeric and muted helpers.
parts.TableCaption: The table caption — its accessible name; can be visually hidden.

features: Native table semantics — every part is the matching HTML element
Three densities, zebra stripes and an optional row hover
Sticky header inside a height-capped scroll container
Horizontal scroll for wide tables, never a broken layout
Numeric cells right-align on tabular numerals
accessibility: Renders native <table>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tr>, <th> and <td>, so row and column relationships come from the platform.
TableHeader defaults to scope="col"; pass scope="row" for a row header.
Give every table a TableCaption (visuallyHidden if the design has no visible title) — it is the table's accessible name.
With label, the scroll container becomes a named region that keyboard users can focus and scroll with the arrow keys.

Scroll the focused region when the table overflows.

components.name: Tree
components.summary: A hierarchical tree view with keyboard navigation, lazy children and optional checkboxes.
components.description:
`Tree` renders a nested set of items as a WAI-ARIA tree: each node can carry an icon, children and a disabled flag. Expanded and selected ids are bindable; set `multiple` for a multi-select tree, or `checkable` for a tri-state checkbox that propagates down to descendants and up to parents.

Children can be loaded lazily the first time a node is opened. Expanding and collapsing is a spring on fractalstyler's `.collapse`, with a quarter-turn caret. Keyboard navigation follows the tree pattern: arrows move, expand and collapse, Home and End jump, typeahead finds a label, and `*` expands every sibling of the focused node.

Optional tri-state checkboxes with parent–child propagation
Lazy loadChildren when a node is first opened
Spring height and a quarter-turn caret

Disabled nodes expose aria-disabled and are skipped by keyboard movement.
When checkable, each node exposes aria-checked (true, false or mixed) and a labelled checkbox.
The expand control on a parent is a labelled button. While children are loading, the node is aria-busy.

components.name: VirtualList
components.summary: A windowed list that keeps 10,000+ rows scrolling smoothly, with an imperative scrollToIndex.
components.description:
`VirtualList` renders only the rows that are on screen, plus a small overscan, so a log, a directory or a long inbox stays light. Positions travel as custom properties through `vars()` — the stage is as tall as every row, and each visible row is placed at its offset — so the stylesheet, not inline styles, owns the layout.

Pass a fixed `itemHeight` when every row is the same height, or an estimator function when they vary; rendered rows are then measured and the offsets catch up. Call `scrollToIndex` on the component instance (via `bind:this`) to jump to a row, aligned to the start, centre or end of the viewport.

features: Windowed rendering for tens of thousands of rows
Fixed heights or an estimator with measurement
Offsets through custom properties, never inline styles
scrollToIndex on the component instance
accessibility: The viewport is a role="list" with an accessible name from label, and is keyboard-scrollable when labelled.
Each visible row is a role="listitem" with aria-setsize and aria-posinset so assistive technology can report position in the full list, not just the window.
Only the visible window is in the DOM; aria-setsize still reflects the full item count.

components.name: BentoGrid
components.summary: A dense, staggered bento grid whose items can span columns and rows, and collapse to one column on small screens.
components.description:
BentoGrid lays tiles on a fixed row height and a chosen column count. Each BentoItem declares how many tracks it occupies; a featured item is raised, and an optional hover lift springs the tile up under the pointer.

Items enter with staggered springs (`stagger()` and `.anim-in`). Column count, gap and row height travel as custom properties, so the stylesheet owns the layout. When the grid's container shrinks below the md measure (28rem), every item drops to a single column.

Give featured tiles their own content — a metric, a chart, a list — and keep unfeatured tiles equally finished; the grid is meant to feel composed, not like a wireframe.

components.name: Masonry
components.summary: A balanced masonry of uneven items, using CSS grid masonry where it is supported and a shortest-column packer everywhere else.
components.description:
Masonry places a list of uneven items into a chosen number of columns. Where the browser supports it, the layout is CSS grid masonry (`grid-template-rows: masonry`). Everywhere else, a JavaScript packer measures the items and sits each one, in source order, in the shortest column. Offsets travel as custom properties (`--x`, `--y`, `--extent`); the stylesheet owns the placement.

Items stay in source order in the DOM, so reading order and tab order are stable even when the visual packing puts a later item into a shorter column. The packer is a fallback, not a second layout to opt into — native masonry and the packer use the same shortest-column rule, so the two paths look the same.

The `columns` prop can be a number, or a map (`base`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`) resolved from the element's width against the system's `--bp-*` breakpoints. Gap and column count travel as custom properties.

components.name: Resizable
components.summary: Split panes that resize by dragging or keyboard, with collapsible panes that spring open and shut.
components.description:
Resizable lays panes side by side or stacked and puts a draggable handle between each pair. Sizes are percentages that always total 100, so the layout survives any container size, and each pane can carry its own minimum, maximum and collapse rules.

Drag a handle with the pointer, move it with the arrow keys, double-click it to return to the default proportions, or press Enter to collapse a collapsible neighbour. Collapsing and expanding spring; dragging follows the pointer directly. `sizes` is bindable, `onResize` reports every change, and `storageKey` remembers the layout between visits.

Give the group a height — it fills its container, so a sized parent is all it needs.

Double-click a handle to restore the default proportions

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: A keyboard-focusable scroll region with thin themed scrollbars and edge fades that appear only when there is more to scroll.
components.description:
ScrollArea is a labelled region that scrolls on one axis or both. Its height can be capped with the measure ladder (xs to 2xl). Scrollbars are thin and themed, and can stay visible, appear on hover and keyboard focus, or be hidden.

Edge fades are scroll-driven: a mask opens at each overflowing edge and closes when that edge is reached, so the fade is never painted over content that is already fully in view. The region is in the tab order and can be scrolled with the keys the platform already provides.

components.name: StickyBar
components.summary: A bar that sticks to the top or bottom of its scroll container and gains glass and elevation only while stuck.
components.description:
StickyBar is for toolbars and save bars. It sits in the document flow and sticks to the top or bottom of its nearest scroll container. A one-pixel sentinel and IntersectionObserver decide when it is stuck; only then does the bar take on glass, a lit rim and elevation.

The offset from the edge is a custom property. The bar is a pop surface (with an enter from the edge it sticks to) so it settles on the same spring tokens as the rest of the library. It does not hide when it is not stuck — a toolbar stays visible, and only its surface changes.

Glass and elevation only while stuck, detected by a sentinel
Configurable offset from the edge
Enters as a pop surface from the stuck edge
accessibility: The bar is a layout structure with no implicit role; put headings, navigation or actions inside it and label them.
Sticking does not remove the bar from the tab order or change its contents.
The sentinel is a decorative 1px probe and is ignored by assistive technology (empty, overflow hidden, not in the tab order).

components.name: AnimatedList
components.summary: A list whose items spring in, out and into their new positions as the data changes.
components.description:
`AnimatedList` is built for a notifications feed: items enter and leave with `springFly`, and the survivors are FLIPped with `createFlip()` so they spring from their old box to their new one. Each item needs a stable `key`; that value is also the `data-flip-id`. Exiting items are taken out of flow with the `.leaving` class (their last box is written to `--ox`, `--oy`, `--ow`) so the rest of the list can settle without a jump.

`max` caps how many items stay visible. With `reverse`, the list is shown newest first and `max` keeps the last items in the source array.

Optional max length

prefers-reduced-motion makes the spring transitions collapse to a short fade and skips FLIP, so items appear and disappear in place.
If an item contains a control (dismiss, open), keep that control labelled; the list itself does not steal focus when items move.

components.name: Draggable
components.summary: A spring-dragged element, with optional bounds, a handle, and keyboard movement.
components.description:
Draggable is the component face of the `drag()` attachment. The element carries `.motion`, `touch-none` and `select-none`, so a pointer drag writes `--mx` and `--my` with rubber-banding, momentum and optional snap-back. A `handle` — a selector or a snippet — limits the pointer to that control; the rest of the element uses `.pointer-none`.

The position is bindable. Arrow keys nudge it (Shift for a longer step), and the element has `aria-roledescription="draggable"`.

Handle as a selector or a snippet
Bindable position with keyboard nudging
Reduced-motion: dragging still works, release settles instantly

Arrow keys move it; Shift multiplies the step. Disabled elements are removed from tab order and expose aria-disabled.
A handle is a visual affordance only — the keyboard still moves the whole element.

components.name: Magnetic
components.summary: Pulls its child toward the pointer, then springs it back.
components.description:
Magnetic wraps any element and attaches the library's `magnetic()` gesture. While the pointer stays within `radius` of the element, it is pulled by `strength`; when the pointer leaves, it springs home. The wrapper carries the `.motion` class so the engine can write `--mx` and `--my`.

The pull is mouse and pen only, and it is disabled under reduced motion — both behaviours come from the attachment itself.

strength, radius and spring are passed through

Reduced-motion safe

The pull is visual only; it does not change click targets in a way that removes a control from the pointer, but a large strength can shift a small target. Keep strength modest on buttons.
Does not respond to the keyboard. Keyboard users reach the child control directly.

components.name: Marquee
components.summary: An infinite scrolling strip of content, with edge fades, pause on hover, and a static fallback under reduced motion.
components.description:
`Marquee` tiles its children into a seamless loop that travels at a constant pixel speed, so a long strip and a short one move at the same pace. The first copy is the one assistive technology reads; every further copy is `aria-hidden` and inert.

`direction` chooses the axis and the sense of travel. `up` and `down` need a container with a height. `fade` masks the edges the content enters and leaves through. `pauseOnHover` stops the loop while the pointer is over the strip or keyboard focus is inside it.

The duration is written as a custom property and honours the motion scale, so `motion="off"` and the reduced-motion preference both freeze the strip into a wrapping row (or column) of the original content.

Pause on hover and keyboard focus
Optional edge fade
Configurable repeat and gap
Reduced motion falls back to a static layout
accessibility: The first copy of the content stays in the document and is read by assistive technology; duplicated copies are aria-hidden and inert, so the list is not announced twice.
The strip pauses while keyboard focus is inside it, so a control or a link in the content can be used without chasing it.
prefers-reduced-motion (and theme motion="off") cancel the animation and lay the content out statically.
The root is a plain div; put a heading or aria-label on it when the strip is a landmark of its own (a ticker, a list of partners).

components.name: Motion
components.summary: A declarative spring element: states layer and animate() springs between them.
components.description:
Motion is the component face of the library's spring engine. You describe states as motion values — `initial`, `animate`, `whileHover`, `whilePress`, `whileFocus`, `whileInView` — and the element resolves them to a single target, then calls `animate()`. Changing a prop mid-flight is interruptible and keeps the current velocity.

Exit is left to Presence. Combining a CSS `out:` transition with the `.motion` channels is not clean — the transition writes `transform` while the engine owns `translate` / `scale` / `opacity` — so unmounting with a spring belongs on `<Presence>`.

features: State layering resolves to one target and calls animate()
Interruptible, velocity-preserving springs
Hover, press, focus and in-view states
Polymorphic as prop
Reduced-motion safe (the engine jumps to the target)
accessibility: Renders the element given by as (a div by default) and forwards every attribute and event to it.
whilePress also responds to Enter and Space when the element is focusable. Pass a native button, or a tabindex, when you use that state.
whileFocus follows focusin/focusout, including focus inside the element.

keyboard.action: Applies whilePress while the key is held, when that state is set and the element is focused.

components.name: NumberTicker
components.summary: A number that springs from zero to its value, as a count or as rolling digit columns.
components.description:
`NumberTicker` drives its display with a `SpringValue`, so a change of `value` is interruptible and keeps its velocity. The formatted final value is always the accessible name (`aria-label`); the ticking glyphs are `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader never hears the count.

`variant="count"` writes the formatted number in tabular numerals. `variant="slot"` splits that string into per-digit rolling columns, driven by the `--digit` custom property on each `.slot`. `format` and `locale` are passed through to `Intl.NumberFormat`. `startOnView` holds the ticker at zero until it crosses into the viewport.

Optional start-when-in-view
The final value is the accessible name

prefers-reduced-motion (and theme motion="off") makes the spring jump to the target, so the final value is shown immediately.
The root is a span. Put it in a heading or a labelled figure when the number is a statistic on the page.

components.name: PageTransition
components.summary: Declarative route transitions for SvelteKit, with a keyed spring fallback when view transitions are unavailable.
components.description:
Pass SvelteKit's `onNavigate` from `$app/navigation` and a `type`. The component renders nothing by itself and calls `setupViewTransitions(onNavigate, { type })` during init, so it belongs in the root layout. `type` may be a fixed `ViewTransitionType` (`fade`, `slide`, `slide-back`, `scale`, `reveal`, `none`) or a function of the navigation — the usual pattern is back → `slide-back`.

The library never imports `$app/*`; the consumer passes the hook in.

```svelte
<script>
	import { onNavigate } from '$app/navigation';
	import { PageTransition } from '@fractaldesign/fractalsvelte-ui';
</script>

<PageTransition {onNavigate} type={(nav) => ((nav.delta ?? 0) < 0 ? 'slide-back' : 'slide')} key={pathname}>
	{@render children()}
</PageTransition>
```

When `key` and children are set and the browser has no view transitions (or reduced motion is on), the children are wrapped in a keyed spring transition (`.overlap`, so the outgoing and incoming views overlap). The spring matches the type: fade, fly for slide / slide-back, scale, blur for reveal, or none. When view transitions are available, route changes are handled by the View Transition API and children render as they are.

features: Wires SvelteKit onNavigate without importing $app
All ViewTransitionType values, or a function of the navigation
Keyed spring fallback when view transitions are missing
Renders nothing when used only as a hook
accessibility: Route transitions are visual only. Focus management stays with the page that is being navigated to; SvelteKit still handles that.
prefers-reduced-motion skips view transitions and the keyed spring fallback, so the new page or panel appears immediately.
type="none" also skips the transition, which is useful when a navigation should not be animated.

components.name: Parallax
components.summary: A scroll-linked offset layer, with a group for stacking a scene at several speeds.
components.description:
`Parallax` offsets its content by `speed` times its distance from the viewport centre. Positive speeds lag behind the scroll (a background feel); negative speeds lead it. `axis` chooses vertical or horizontal travel.

Where the platform supports CSS scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline: view()`), the layer uses the `.parallax-view` fast path and the `--speed` custom property. Everywhere else it uses the `parallax()` attachment and the `.motion` channels. Reduced motion cancels the offset in both paths.

`ParallaxGroup` is a clipped, relatively positioned frame for stacking several layers into one scene.

CSS scroll-driven animation fast path where supported
JavaScript parallax() attachment fallback
ParallaxGroup for layered scenes
Reduced motion cancels the offset
accessibility: Parallax is decorative motion around existing content. The content stays in the document and is read in source order, regardless of its visual offset.
prefers-reduced-motion (and theme motion="off") holds every layer at rest, on both the CSS and JavaScript paths.
Keep essential text on a slow or zero-speed layer so it remains readable while other layers move.

components.name: Presence
components.summary: Mounts and unmounts children with spring enter and exit transitions.
components.description:
Presence is the unmounting counterpart to Motion. Pass `show` to play a spring enter or exit — fade, scale, fly, blur or slide — built on the library's `spring*` transition functions. A `key` treats a change of children as a swap; `mode="sync"` crosses the two, and `mode="wait"` holds the enter until the exit has finished.

Use it whenever something must leave the document, not just change pose: a dismissed notice, a swapped panel, a collapsing footnote.

features: Eight enter and exit presets, all spring-eased
Keyed swaps in sync or wait mode
onExitComplete after the exit has finished
Reduced-motion safe (the transitions collapse to a short fade)
accessibility: Renders a wrapping div around the children while they are present, and forwards attributes to it.
The children are removed from the document after the exit transition, so they leave the accessibility tree once they have finished leaving.
Does not manage focus. Move focus before hiding a dialog or a similar surface that had it.

components.name: Reorder
components.summary: A drag-to-reorder list whose siblings make room with FLIP springs.
components.description:
Reorder is a generic list. Bind `items`, pass a `key` accessor, and render each row with the `children` snippet — it receives the item and `{ dragging, handleProps }`. Pointer drags lift the row (scale and shadow) while `createFlip()` springs the others aside. Keyboard users lift with Space, move with the arrows, drop with Space, and cancel with Escape.

Announcements go through a live region, following the WAI-ARIA drag-and-drop list pattern.

Pointer drag with a lifted item
Keyboard reordering with live-region announcements
Bindable items and an onReorder callback
Horizontal or vertical axis
accessibility: The list is a listbox with aria-roledescription="sortable list". Each row is an option with aria-grabbed and aria-selected.
A visually hidden description explains the keyboard, and an assertive live region announces grabs, moves, drops and cancellations.
Roving tabindex keeps a single tab stop in the list. Focus is restored to the moved item after a keyboard reorder.

Moves focus between items, or moves a lifted item along the list axis.
Lifts the focused item, or drops it if it is already lifted.

components.name: Reveal
components.summary: Springs its contents in when they scroll into view.
components.description:
Reveal watches the viewport with `inView()` and springs the element from an offset state to rest, the same way the `reveal()` attachment does. `direction` and `distance` set the offset, and optional `scale` and `blur` join the spring.

Blur is not a channel on `reveal()` itself, so when `blur` is set the component writes a `--blur` custom property and the kit's `.blur-in` class owns the filter. Use `once={false}` when the element should spring back out as it leaves.

features: Scroll-triggered entrance on inView()
Direction, distance, scale and blur
once and amount match the reveal() attachment
Reduced-motion safe: the element is shown at rest
accessibility: Renders a wrapping div and forwards attributes to it.
The content is always in the document — only its motion changes — so it stays in the accessibility tree while off-screen.
Under reduced motion the element appears at rest with no offset or blur.

components.name: ScrollProgress
components.summary: A reading-progress bar or ring, bound to the page or to an element as it passes through the viewport.
components.description:
`ScrollProgress` uses the `scrollProgress()` attachment to write `--value` (0 to 1) and paints it with `.fill` or `.ring`. `target="page"` tracks the document; `target="element"` tracks this component's own passage through the viewport (0 as it enters, 1 as it leaves), so a bar can follow a single article.

The bar is a hairline along the top or bottom of the viewport and grows by scale (`.fill.scaled`), not width, so it stays on the compositor. The ring uses the shared `.ring` conic fill. `tone` re-points `--theme-color` so both follow the same status colour.

Page scroll or element passage
Top or bottom bar position
Five tones
Compositor-only bar (scale, not width)
accessibility: The meter is a progressbar labelled "Reading progress". The value is visual; the bar does not announce every scroll tick, which would be noisy.
prefers-reduced-motion does not hide the meter: progress still updates, without introducing animation of its own (the attachment writes --value directly).
Place the component around an article when target is element, so the accessible name describes that reading, or pass aria-label to override it.

components.name: SharedElement
components.summary: Gives an element a view-transition identity so it can morph between routes or in-page states.
components.description:
`SharedElement` writes a view-transition name onto its element (`vtName()` plus the `.vt-name` class). Two elements that use the same `name` — a grid card on one view, a detail hero on the next — morph from one box to the other when a view transition runs.

For in-page state changes (a card expanding in place, a grid becoming a detail) call the exported `morph(update, options)` helper, which wraps `startViewTransition`. On browsers without the API, or under reduced motion, `update` is applied directly and the change is instant.

features: View-transition identity via vtName() and .vt-name
Works across routes and in-page state changes
morph() helper wrapping startViewTransition
Renders as any tag
accessibility: The component does not change the accessibility tree: it is the same element with a view-transition name. Keep headings, labels and focus management in the content you render.
prefers-reduced-motion makes morph() apply the state change without a transition, so the new view is shown immediately.
After an in-page morph, move focus to the new view when it is a dialog or a detail pane, so keyboard users are not left on a control that has been replaced.

components.name: Stagger
components.summary: Reveals its children in sequence, staggered from first, last or centre.
components.description:
Stagger writes `--i` on each direct child and `--stagger` on the group, then adds `.anim-in` (on mount) or `.reveal` (when `trigger="inView"`) together with an `.enter-*` preset. The delay is `calc(var(--i) * var(--stagger))`, so the same CSS the rest of the library uses does the work.

The `slide` preset uses `.enter-edge-bottom`, which is the CSS counterpart of a slide-from-edge entrance. Height-collapsing `springSlide` belongs on Presence, where it can run as a Svelte transition.

features: stagger() writes --i and --stagger
from first, last or centre
Trigger on mount or when the group is in view
Eight enter presets, matching Presence
accessibility: Renders a wrapping div around the children and forwards attributes to it.
The children stay in the document; only their entrance is delayed. They remain in the accessibility tree while waiting to appear.
Under reduced motion, stagger() writes --stagger: 0ms, so every child appears together.

components.name: TextReveal
components.summary: Text that enters one character, word or line at a time, staggered on the `--i` channel.
components.description:
`TextReveal` splits a string into pieces and plays `.anim-in` on each one, staggered by the `--i` channel and `stagger()`. `preset` chooses the entrance (`fade-up`, `blur`, `scale`, or `slide`) through the shared `.enter-*` classes. `trigger="inView"` holds the pieces at their first frame (`.held`) until the text crosses into the viewport.

The full string stays the accessible name of the wrapper (`aria-label`); every visual piece is `aria-hidden`, so assistive technology reads the sentence once, not as a stream of letters.

Four entrance presets
Configurable stagger step
Mount or in-view trigger
Renders as any tag
accessibility: The wrapper carries aria-label set to the full string. Each visual piece is aria-hidden, so the text is announced once rather than letter by letter.
prefers-reduced-motion collapses the staggered animation (the motion scale is already applied to .anim-in).
Choose `as` so the text is the right heading or paragraph for the page; the default is a paragraph.

components.name: TiltCard
components.summary: Tilts a card in 3D toward the pointer, with an optional glare highlight.
components.description:
TiltCard attaches the library's `tilt()` gesture. The element carries `.tilt` and `.motion`, so the engine can write `--rx`, `--ry` and a lift `--ms`. When `glare` is on, `tilt()` also writes `--px` and `--py` as percentages, and a `.glare` layer — a kit fragment primitive — paints a highlight at that point.

The tilt is disabled under reduced motion by the attachment itself.

Optional glare following --px and --py
max, scale and spring are passed through
Reduced-motion safe

The glare layer is decorative, pointer-events none, and is not exposed to assistive technology.
The tilt is visual only and does not affect keyboard use. Focused content inside the card is unchanged.

components.name: Typewriter
components.summary: Types and deletes its way through a list of words, with a blinking caret.
components.description:
`Typewriter` types each string in `words`, holds it for `pause` milliseconds, then deletes it and moves on. `speed` and `deleteSpeed` are the milliseconds spent on each character. With `loop`, it returns to the first word after the last is deleted; without it, the last word stays.

The first word is in the HTML on the server, so the line is never empty before hydration. The animated glyphs are `aria-hidden` and `aria-live="off"`; a static `aria-label` on the wrapper lists every word, so a screen reader is not read a stream of keystrokes.

Configurable type speed, delete speed and pause
Optional looping
Optional blinking caret

accessibility: The wrapper carries a static aria-label listing every word. The typed text is aria-hidden and aria-live="off", so assistive technology does not hear characters appearing and disappearing.
prefers-reduced-motion (and theme motion="off") shows the first word immediately and does not type or delete. The caret uses .anim-blink, which the motion layer cancels under reduced motion.
The root is a span. Place it inside a heading or a sentence so the static label reads naturally.

Aurora paints two overlapping, heavily blurred colour fields whose hues are offset from the current `--hue`. They drift on a transform, so the motion stays on the compositor, and they pause under reduced motion — the fields remain, they just stop moving.

Children are rendered on top. Intensity and speed are written as custom properties, so the same section can sit quietly behind a hero or move a little more on a feature band.

Children sit above the fields
Pauses under reduced motion, GPU-friendly transforms

components.description:

The beam is a narrow slice of a conic gradient, masked to a 1px border and rotated through the same registered `--angle` as the glow card. `duration`, `size`, `delay` and `reverse` are written as custom properties; the motion pauses under reduced motion.

Follows the parent border radius
Decorative: aria-hidden and pointer-events none

components.name: Noise

components.name: SpotlightCard
components.summary: A card lit by a soft radial light that follows the pointer, on the surface and along the border.
components.description:
A spotlight card is an ordinary raised surface with a pointer-following light. The `pointer()` attachment writes `--px` and `--py` as unitless fractions; a kit primitive paints a radial wash on the surface and a matching highlight on the 1px border.

The light is theme-coloured by default, or a neutral white highlight. It is clipped to the card, sits under the content, and does nothing under a fine pointer — the last position, or the centre, remains until the pointer moves.

features: Surface light and border highlight follow the pointer
Configurable light size and intensity
Theme accent or a neutral white highlight
GPU-friendly: custom properties only, contain: paint
accessibility: The light is painted with decorative pseudo-elements, so it is not exposed to assistive technology. The card content is the accessible content.
The effect does not capture pointer events and does not change the role of the card.

components.name: ModeToggle
components.summary: Switches between light, dark and system mode with a circular reveal from the click point.
components.description:
A view over the shared `theme`. Pressing it calls `theme.toggleMode(event)` (or `theme.setMode(mode, event)`), so the new mode wipes in as a circular view transition that grows from where you clicked. Keyboard activation reveals from the centre of the control. The sun and moon swap on a spring and settle instantly under reduced motion.

Pick the shape that fits the surface: an `icon` button for toolbars, a `switch` for settings rows, or a `segmented` group when `system` should be visible. Add `withSystem` to offer the OS preference.

Leave `value` out to drive the shared theme. Pass a `value` and the component only reports changes through `value` and `onValueChange`, still with the reveal, which suits a provider-scoped or stored preference.

features: Three shapes: icon button, switch, segmented radio group
Optional system mode
Circular view-transition reveal from the pointer
Spring sun / moon swap
accessibility: The icon button is a native button with aria-pressed reflecting dark mode and a fixed aria-label; with `withSystem` it is a three-step cycle whose label names the current and next mode instead.
The switch has role="switch" with aria-checked set while dark mode is on.
The segmented form is a radiogroup of radios with a roving tab stop; arrow keys move and select.
Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

In the segmented group, selects the first or last mode.

components.name: ThemeCustomizer
components.summary: The live theme editor: mode, named theme, colour, radius, density, motion, a preview, and copy or reset.
components.description:
The proof of complete customisability. Every axis of the theme is here — light, dark or system mode, the named themes, hue (0–360 on a hue-gradient track), chroma, tint, three radii, three densities and four motion profiles — plus a live preview of sample surfaces and buttons.

Leave `value` out to drive the shared `theme`. Pass a `value` to keep the edits inside a preview (pair it with `ThemeProvider`) so the surrounding page is undisturbed. `sections` hides any block you do not need.

Reset returns to the defaults. Copy CSS emits the `data-*` attributes and any custom properties; Copy config emits the `ThemeSettings` JSON. Both confirm on the button when the clipboard accepts the text.

features: Mode, named theme, hue, chroma, tint, radius, density and motion
Live preview strip
sections to choose which controls to show
Reset, Copy CSS and Copy config, with clipboard feedback
Controlled or shared-theme operation
accessibility: Every slider is a native range input with an accessible name. Radius, density and motion are radiogroups of radios.
Mode and theme reuse ModeToggle and ThemePicker, including their keyboard behaviour.
Copy and Reset are named buttons; the copy buttons announce success by changing their label to “Copied CSS” or “Copied config”.
The preview is a themed subtree and is not a live region, so moving a slider does not interrupt a screen reader.

components.name: ThemeProvider
components.summary: Themes a subtree independently of the page, or the whole document with `root`.
components.description:
The theme is plain attributes and three numbers, so any element can carry it. `ThemeProvider` renders a wrapper with the `data-theme`, `data-mode`, `data-shape`, `data-density` and `data-motion` attributes you ask for, and writes `hue`, `chroma` and `tint` as the custom properties `--hue`, `--chroma` and `--tint`. Everything inside re-themes at once: colours, corner radii, spacing and motion. Anything you leave out is inherited from the page.

Use it for a light card on a dark page, a brand-coloured panel, a compact toolbar, or a live preview that must not disturb the surrounding page.

For the whole document use `<ThemeProvider root>` once in the root layout. It calls `initTheme()` (restores the saved theme, follows the OS colour scheme and keeps `<html>` and `localStorage` in step with the shared `theme`) and also inlines `themeInitScript()` in `<svelte:head>`, so the saved mode is applied before first paint and there is no flash. Calling `initTheme()` directly in the layout script works the same way; then add `<script>{@html themeInitScript()}</script>` to `<svelte:head>` yourself. In SvelteKit, `app.html` is the other place for the script.

features: Themes any subtree: theme, mode, hue, chroma, tint, radius, density and motion
Unset axes inherit from the page, including customised hue, chroma and tint
Numeric overrides travel as custom properties, never inline styles
`root` themes the document: restore, persist, follow the OS, no flash
Renders as div, section, article or aside
accessibility: The wrapper is a plain element with no role; choose `as` to give it the right landmark (`section`, `aside`, `article`).
`system` mode follows the OS preference and respects the user's choice of colour scheme.
`motion="off"` removes spring motion inside the subtree; the reduced-motion preference is always honoured on top of it.
Contrast is designed per mode: every text colour role keeps its contrast against the surfaces of the same mode.
